To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the identity function of differentiation (obtaining an identity) was most prominent in minimal groups and that the instrumental function of differentiation (advancing group interests) was most prominent when group goals were salient.

(1) intergroup differentiation can have two distinct functions, an identity function and an instrumental function, and (2) these two functions of differentiation are differentially promoted in different contexts, and (3) the two functions of differentiation can be distinguished in terms of their consequences, and (4) the identity function is more important in minimal groups, whereas the instrumental function is more important when the group has a goal.

(a) the possibility of differentiation and the presence of group goals interact to determine the strength of differentiation, (b) the identity function of intergroup differentiation is more likely to occur when differentiation is not possible, and (c) the instrumental function of intergroup differentation occurs when group goals are important and differentiation is possible.
